subtitle: How a Hill Chief Forged the Ruby Line of Tripura

panels.action: Chhengthung Fa (Maha Manikya) stands on a windswept Tripura ridge, hand resting on a simple sword, behind him terraced hills fade toward the Bengal plains as storm clouds gather over distant mosques and forests.

dialogue.text: In the misty hills between Bengal and the sea, Chhengthung Fa took the name Manikya—and turned a scattered land into a kingdom that would endure for centuries.

i18n.hi: बंगाल और सागर के बीच धुंधली पहाड़ियों में छेंगथुंग फ़ा ने मनिक्य नाम लिया—and बिखरी धरती को सदियों टिकने वाला राज्य बना दिया।

panels.action: A dawn panorama of the Tripura hills c.1400 CE: dense forests, shifting jhum fields, bamboo hamlets clinging to ridges, and far away the flat, flooded Bengal plains with tiny minarets and caravan trails.

dialogue.text: Around 1400, the Tripura hills were a patchwork of clans and clearings, jhum fields and bamboo forts, balanced between the forested uplands and the rich, restless plains of Bengal.

i18n.hi: लगभग 1400 में त्रिपुरा की पहाड़ियाँ कुलों और खेड़ों की रंग-बिरंगी चादर थीं—झूम के खेत, बाँस के किले, ऊपर जंगल, नीचे उफनता समृद्ध बंगाल मैदान।

panels.action: Young Chhengthung Fa sits in a bamboo council house lit by firelight, listening intently as elder chiefs of different Tripuri clans argue, their ornaments and hairstyles subtly distinct, a map of hills drawn on a leaf mat before them.

dialogue.text: Rajmala, the court chronicle, remembers Chhengthung Fa as a hill chief among chiefs, born into the line that claimed these ridges, yet still needing to persuade rival Tripuri houses to follow his standard.

i18n.hi: राजमाला, दरबारी इतिहास, छेंगथुंग फ़ा को सरदारों में पहाड़ी सरदार मानती है—जन्म से इन पहाड़ियों का दावेदार, पर फिर भी प्रतिद्वंद्वी त्रिपुरी घरानों को अपने झंडे तले लाने की जद्दोजहद में।

panels.action: Chhengthung Fa rises from his seat in the council house, one hand spread over the rough map of the hills, the other resting on a spear, while some elders lean forward and others look away, undecided.

dialogue.speaker: chhengthung_fa
dialogue.text: If we stand apart, the hills will fall one village at a time.

i18n.hi: हम बिखरे रहे तो पहाड़ गाँव–गाँव गिरेंगे।

panels.action: Chhengthung Fa moves through misty forest paths with a small escort, greeting Kukis on one ridge, Jamatias in a palisaded village, and Reang elders near a riverbank, each scene showing different dress and weapons while he speaks calmly.

dialogue.text: The Rajmala says he subdued Kukis, Jamatias, Reangs—tribal polities along the ridges. Whether through battle, alliance, or both, later memory insists that under him the hill peoples began to march under one authority.

i18n.hi: राजमाला कहती है कि उसने कूकी, जमातिया, रींग—इन पहाड़ी राजनियों को वश में किया। लड़ाई से, मेल से, या दोनों से—याद बस इतना बचा कि उसके नीचे पहाड़ी जन एक ही हुकूमत के नीचे चलने लगे।

panels.action: On a cleared hilltop, Tripuri warriors in bamboo armor clash with another hill band; no wounds are shown, only shields locked, spears braced, and Chhengthung Fa standing firm at the center, raising his arm in a signal to stop as the opponents begin to yield.

dialogue.text: War left scars, but the chronicle speaks more of outcomes than details: ridges once independent accepted tribute, and a single court began to speak for the hills to the world beyond.

i18n.hi: युद्ध ने घाव छोड़े, पर इतिहास जीत पर ज़्यादा बोलता है, जख़्मों पर कम—जो धारियाँ खुद मालिक थीं, अब नज़राना देती हैं, और एक ही दरबार पहाड़ियों की ओर से बाहरी दुनिया से बोलने लगता है।

panels.action: Chhengthung Fa stands by a riverine frontier outpost: stockades overlook a flat plain where Bengali farmers till fields and a distant mosque rises; he watches a Bengal caravan pass, a mix of traders and armed men, his face tense.

dialogue.text: To the west lay the Bengal Sultanate, with cavalry, coins, and chroniclers. Between their plains and his hills, grazing and trade routes became lines of friction the Rajmala would later call a frontier incident.

i18n.hi: पश्चिम में था बंगाल सल्तनत—घुड़सवार, सिक्के, इतिहासकार। उनके मैदान और इन पहाड़ियों के बीच चरागाह और व्यापार के रास्ते ऐसी रगड़ की लकीर बने, जिसे राजमाला बाद में सरहदी टक्कर कहेगी।

panels.action: Close on Chhengthung Fa’s weathered face by firelight as a scout whispers in his ear, his eyes narrowing, jaw set, the shadows of armored horsemen flickering in the background.

dialogue.text: The dynasty’s memory says that after a clash on this border, a Bengal Sultanate force came into the hills. No Bengal chronicler confirms it, yet in Tripura’s own record this threat looms over his story.

i18n.hi: वंश की यादों के अनुसार, सीमा पर टकराव के बाद बंगाल सल्तनत की फौज पहाड़ियों में घुसी। बंगाल के इतिहास इससे चुप हैं, पर त्रिपुरा की किताब में यही ख़तरा उसके किस्से पर मंडराता रहता है।

panels.action: On a forest edge opening to a plain, Tripuri warriors line up with bows and spears, light armor of cane and cloth, while Chhengthung Fa rides or stands at the front; in the distance a disciplined line of Bengal cavalry approaches, pennants fluttering.

dialogue.text: Rajmala tells of battle: Bengal cavalry pressing into unfamiliar forests, hill archers and spearmen using ridges and ravines. The details are legend, but the memory that hills could resist plains power became central to Tripura’s pride.

i18n.hi: राजमाला लड़ाई का हाल सुनाती है—अनजाने जंगलों में धँसती बंगाली सवारियाँ, और पहाड़ी धनुर्धर–भाला लेकर, ढाल–खाईं को हथियार बनाते हुए। दास्तान चाहे बढ़ा–चढ़ा हो, पर यह याद कि पहाड़ मैदान के दमखम को रोक सकते हैं, त्रिपुरा की शान का दिल बन गई।

panels.action: In a thick bamboo grove, silhouettes of mounted men falter among tangled roots and felled trunks, while Chhengthung Fa signals silently from a slope, his warriors poised along hidden paths, the moment suspended just before the two sides meet.

dialogue.speaker: chhengthung_fa
dialogue.text: Let the forest fight for us.

i18n.hi: जंगल को हमारे लिए लड़ने दो।

panels.action: After the battle, smoke or mist hangs over the clearing; Bengal horsemen withdraw toward the plains, while Tripuri warriors stand weary but unbroken around Chhengthung Fa, who plants his spear in the earth and looks toward the setting sun over Bengal.

dialogue.text: The Rajmala gives the victory to Chhengthung Fa. However we weigh its accuracy, by the time the chronicle was written, this story marked the moment the hills claimed parity with their powerful neighbor.

i18n.hi: राजमाला जीत छेंगथुंग फ़ा के नाम लिखती है। सच–झूठ जैसा भी हो, जब तक किताब लिखी गई, यह किस्सा वही पल बन गया जब पहाड़ ने अपने ताक़तवर पड़ोसी के बराबर होने का दावा किया।

panels.action: Inside a simple yet dignified bamboo hall, Chhengthung Fa sits on a wooden platform; before him, artisans present a new crown with a single ruby-like gem, while priests and elders watch, the atmosphere solemn but intimate.

dialogue.text: Then everything changed in the way he was named. Later coins and scholars like N.N. Bhattacharyya show that the Manikya title, tied to the image of a ruby, emerged with these early rulers, not only with the later Ratna Manikya.

i18n.hi: फिर उसके नाम में ही सब कुछ बदल गया। बाद के सिक्कों और एन.एन. भट्टाचार्य जैसे विद्वानों से पता चलता है कि माणिक यानी रूबी से जुड़ी मनिक्य उपाधि इन्हीं शुरुआती राजाओं के साथ उभरी, अकेले बाद के रत्न मनिक्य से नहीं।

panels.action: Close on Chhengthung Fa’s hands lifting the modest crown set with a single gleaming red stone, his fingers rough from campaign and travel, the gem catching a shaft of light in the dark hall.

dialogue.speaker: chhengthung_fa
dialogue.text: A name must bind more strongly than fear.

i18n.hi: नाम को डर से ज़्यादा मज़बूती से बाँधना होगा।

panels.action: Chhengthung Fa, now wearing the crown with the ruby, sits formally enthroned; clan leaders of various Tripuri groups kneel or bow in their own styles, bringing tokens—bows, grain, ornaments—as the hall fills with quiet expectation.

dialogue.text: Rajmala remembers him as Maha Manikya—the Great Manikya. Whether the word came from a literal ruby or a metaphor for precious authority, it turned a hill chief into the founder of a named dynasty.

i18n.hi: राजमाला उसे महा मनिक्य—महान मनिक्य—कहती है। रूबी सचमुच की थी या कीमती सत्ता का रूपक, इससे फर्क नहीं पड़ा—एक पहाड़ी सरदार ही में नाम–धारी वंश का संस्थापक दिखने लगा।

panels.action: Chhengthung Fa consults with scribes and a metalworker; on a low table lie clay impressions and a freshly struck coin showing early symbols and the Manikya name, while outside the open wall, traders and villagers gather.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, historians like Ramani Mohan Sarma would study these coins. Their inscriptions quietly correct the Rajmala’s ordering, revealing that the Manikya name was already in use before the more famous Ratna.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद रमणी मोहन शर्मा जैसे इतिहासकार इन सिक्कों को पढ़ेंगे। इनके लेख quietly राजमाला की क्रम–सूची सुधारते हैं—दिखाते हैं कि मशहूर रत्न से पहले ही मनिक्य नाम चलन में था।

panels.action: A visual montage radiates from Chhengthung Fa’s throne: hill villages paying tax, soldiers drilling on terraces, envoys travelling toward a distant cityscape of the Bengal plains, and a faint overlay of Chinese scrolls hinting at Ming Shilu references.

dialogue.text: Beyond legend, external eyes also noticed. Ming Shilu, the Chinese imperial record, later spoke of Di-wu-la—Tripura—signaling that a polity in these hills was dealing with distant courts as well as nearby sultanates.

i18n.hi: किंवदंती से परे, बाहरी नज़रें भी चौकन्नी थीं। मिंग शिलु, चीनी शाही दफ्तरी रिकॉर्ड, बाद में दी-वू-ला—त्रिपुरा—का ज़िक्र करता है, इशारा कि यह पहाड़ी राज सिर्फ पास के सल्तनतों नहीं, दूर दरबारों से भी सौदा कर रहा था।

panels.action: In twilight on the same ridge as the cover, an older Chhengthung Fa sits on a rock, crown resting beside him, watching smoke rise from peaceful hill villages and the faint lanterns of the plains beyond, his expression calm but searching.

dialogue.text: Chhengthung Fa’s life recedes in mist; his dates are pieced together from coins, chronicles, and echoes. But the kingdom he named would carry the Manikya title down five centuries of wars, alliances, and changing worlds.

i18n.hi: छेंगथुंग फ़ा की ज़िंदगी धुंध में खोती जाती है—तारीखें सिक्कों, किताबों और गूँजों से जोड़ी गईं। पर जो राज्य उसने नाम दिया, वही मनिक्य उपाधि को पाँच सदियों तक युद्धों, साँठ–गाँठों और बदलती दुनिया में ढोता रहा।

panels.action: A weathered Manikya coin lies half-buried on a forest floor; above it, out of focus, children from different Tripuri communities play together on a hillside, bamboo houses and a modern skyline faint in the far distance.

dialogue.text: In the end, his story is less about one man than about a moment when scattered hill peoples accepted a shared ruby name—and discovered that a standard, once raised, can outlast the hand that first held it.

i18n.hi: अंत में उसकी दास्तान एक आदमी से कम, उस घड़ी के बारे में ज़्यादा है—जब बिखरी पहाड़ियाँ एक साझा रूबी नाम पर राज़ी हुईं, और जाना कि झंडा एक बार उठ जाए तो उसे थामने वाला हाथ मिटकर भी झंडा जिंदा रह सकता है।

title_i18n.en: Chhengthung Fa Takes the Manikya Name
title_i18n.hi: छेंगथुंग फ़ा ने मनिक्य उपाधि अपनाई

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Hill Chief Forged the Ruby Line of Tripura
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक पहाड़ी सरदार ने त्रिपुरा की रूबी वंश रचा
